sections.heading: Glossary term: Tide
sections.body: On Earth, the gravitational force is almost constant, pointing what we call downwards. But over larger distances, gravity's strength and direction vary, and those differences are called tidal forces. The Earth and the Moon, for instance, orbit a common center of mass due to their mutual gravitational attraction, but objects on the side of Earth nearer the Moon will be accelerated a bit more strongly towards the Moon, objects on the opposite side of Earth somewhat less. Earth's ocean water follows those tidal accelerations, forming "tidal bulges" directly under the Moon and on the opposite side, which produces Earth's tides.

sections.source_html:
Glossary term: Tide

Description: On Earth, the gravitational force is almost constant, pointing what we call downwards. But over larger distances, gravity's strength and direction vary, and those differences are called tidal forces. The Earth and the Moon, for instance, orbit a common center of mass due to their mutual gravitational attraction, but objects on the side of Earth nearer the Moon will be accelerated a bit more strongly towards the Moon, objects on the opposite side of Earth somewhat less. Earth's ocean water follows those tidal accelerations, forming "tidal bulges" directly under the Moon and on the opposite side, which produces Earth's tides.

Related Terms:

  • Gravity
  • Tidal Locking


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

If you notice a factual error in this glossary definition then please get in touch.
sections.body_ru: На Земле гравитационная сила почти постоянна и направлена в ту сторону, которую мы называем «вниз». Но на больших расстояниях величина и направление силы гравитации меняются, и эти различия называются приливными силами. Земля и Луна, например, обращаются вокруг общего центра масс благодаря взаимному гравитационному притяжению, но объекты на стороне Земли, ближайшей к Луне, получают несколько большее ускорение в направлении Луны, а объекты на противоположной стороне Земли — несколько меньшее. Под действием этих приливных ускорений в океанах Земли образуются «приливные горбы» непосредственно под Луной и на противоположной стороне, что вызывает приливы на Земле.
